purpose: Determine whether the LongHorizon-Harness implementation can avoid duplicate authoring of an operational long-horizon coordinator while preserving Agent Autonomy Harness ownership of end-to-end process-fidelity, authority, verification, and lifecycle acceptance.

taskContract.useCase: Reduce process loss from requirements through delivery by carrying audited progress, bounded next-step contracts, evidence, and human intervention gates across fresh execution contexts.
taskContract.currentGap: The repository has broad process-fidelity protocols and stop-authoring rules but no admitted operational Manage-Execute-Audit coordinator whose behavior, authority boundary, recovery, and value are accepted.
taskContract.sourceBoundary: The named X post, arXiv v1 paper, project site, and public AMAP-ML repository at one exact revision; no child-source expansion or benchmark payload acquisition.
taskContract.accountAndDataBoundary: Public source metadata and Git objects only; no account connection, private data, credential use, model prompt, task payload, or consumer workspace access.
taskContract.authorityBoundary: Static read-only review and repository-owned evidence recording only; no installation, enablement, execution, model dispatch, consumer mutation, manager substitution, fork, publication, or release.
taskContract.verificationSurface: Exact revision and selected Git object identities, MIT license metadata, source-to-mechanism anchors, explicit author-reported benchmark limits, Harness fit mapping, adoption blockers, and deterministic boundary validation.

xPost.role: user-bound discovery and secondary summary source
xPost.claimAuthority: not implementation, license, or benchmark authority

paper.title: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks

repository.licenseDisposition: Core repository code is MIT; vendored benchmark subtrees retain separate license or notice boundaries and were not acquired or admitted.

sourceSnapshot.retrievalMethod: official pages plus public Git refs and GitHub Git-object metadata; no clone, package download, install, or third-party execution

mechanismFindings.finding: Manager, fresh-context Executor, and separate Auditor form an implemented bounded loop rather than a paper-only concept.
Task state, task contract, audit reports, trajectories, events, and round records provide inspectable within-run continuity.
A done route is rejected without a complete, clean, aligned latest audit; ask, blocked, and maximum-round routes remain explicit.
The adapter layer delegates the underlying agent loop to Claude Code or Codex and is a plausible comparison seam.
Task state and task contract are persisted and parsed as natural-language control artifacts rather than a fully typed requirement, evidence, and authority transition model.

reportedBenchmarkObservations.admissibleConclusion: The author-reported results justify a bounded comparison candidate, not behavior, value, efficiency, portability, or production claims for Agent Autonomy Harness.

adoptionBlockers.finding: Default adapter commands bypass native permission, approval, or sandbox controls.
Claude workspace mutation is detected and invalidated after execution rather than prevented or restored, and no equivalent Codex role-enforcement seam was verified.
Persisted run artifacts were verified, but no command or replay path that resumes an earlier interrupted manager loop was found.

The project is new, describes Windows as not thoroughly tested, has no independent top-level core-package test suite at the revision, and the visible workflow builds or publishes without running core tests.

harnessFit.stopAuthoringDecision: Do not self-author an equivalent operational long-horizon coordinator before this exact-revision candidate is mapped and falsified against explicit residual gaps.
harnessFit.nextGate: Map the exact state, contract, audit, event, adapter, permission, recovery, and comparison seams to the current process-fidelity protocol and acceptance subgates without installing or executing the project.
